_comment: OpenSSF Best Practices badge (passing level) proposed answers for Withe. Read by bestpractices.dev when the project entry is edited or re-run with 'Save (and continue)'. Status values: Met | Unmet | N/A ('?' / unknown are ignored, leaving any existing answer unchanged). Justifications are a starting point; the authorized maintainer reviews and confirms each before saving. Project: https://www.bestpractices.dev/en/projects/14108 - Repository: https://github.com/schubydoo/withe
description_good_justification: The README and the documentation site describe what Withe does - a read-only web dashboard for the Renovate CE you already run - before anything else. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe
interact_justification: Users can ask questions and interact through GitHub Issues. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/issues
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md at the repository root explains how to contribute. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements: open an issue first for anything larger than a bug fix, one change per pull request, Conventional Commit subjects, green CI (types, lint, unit and end-to-end tests), a changeset for any user-visible change, and WCAG 2.1 AA for user-facing changes. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_justification: Released under the MIT License, an OSI-approved and FSF-recognized FLOSS license. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open source license.
license_location_justification: The license is in the standard top-level LICENSE file. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: The README and a versioned MkDocs documentation site cover installation, configuration, and usage. https://schubydoo.github.io/withe/
documentation_interface_justification: The documentation describes the external interface: the read-only web dashboard, the environment-variable configuration (WITHE_CE_URL, WITHE_CE_TOKEN, WITHE_AUTH_USER/PASS), and the container deployment. https://schubydoo.github.io/withe/
sites_https_justification: The repository (github.com), the documentation site (schubydoo.github.io), and the image registry (ghcr.io) are served exclusively over HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests provide searchable, URL-addressable discussion that needs no client-side JavaScript. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/issues
english_justification: All documentation and code comments are in English.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained; changes ship through reviewed pull requests, and v1.0.0 has been released.
repo_public_justification: The source is in a public git repository. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe
repo_track_justification: git records what changed, who changed it, and when.
repo_interim_justification: Interim development versions are public between releases as commits and pull requests on GitHub.
repo_distributed_justification: The project uses git, a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version identifier, held in package.json and the matching git tag (e.g. v1.0.0).
version_tags_justification: Every release is an SSH-signed git tag of the form vX.Y.Z, cut by the automated knope release workflow; tag creation and movement are locked down by a tag-protection ruleset. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/tags
release_notes_justification: Each release has human-readable notes: knope generates a curated, grouped CHANGELOG.md entry and a matching tagged GitHub Release from per-change .changeset fragments. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in a released version to date; the changelog reserves a dedicated security category (via knope changesets) for such fixes when they occur.
report_process_justification: The process for reporting bugs (GitHub Issues) is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and the issue tracker. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/issues
report_tracker_justification: Bugs are tracked in GitHub Issues.
report_responses_justification: The maintainer monitors the issue tracker and responds to bug reports; the project is new and has no backlog of unanswered reports.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests filed as GitHub Issues receive a response, including a decision when a request falls outside Withe's deliberately narrow scope (the README lists the permanent exclusions).
report_archive_justification: The bug-report history is publicly archived and searchable in GitHub Issues. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/issues
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the vulnerability reporting process. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Vulnerabilities are reported privately through GitHub private security advisories. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging a vulnerability report within 7 days.
build_justification: The project builds from source: `npm ci` then `npm run build` (Next.js), and a Dockerfile produces the container image.
build_common_tools_justification: It is built with common, widely available FLOSS tools (Node.js, npm, Next.js).
build_floss_tools_justification: All build tooling (Node.js, npm, Next.js, esbuild) is FLOSS.
test_justification: An automated test suite runs with `npm test` (node --test), offline.
test_invocation_justification: Tests run with the standard `npm test`, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/schubydoo/withe/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_most_justification: The suite covers most of the code (~98% of lines), enforced by a CI coverage floor (90% lines / 80% branches / 85% functions).
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the full suite on every pull request and push to main.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for new functionality, backed by the merge-blocking coverage floor.
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality is added with tests; the coverage floor blocks merges that would drop coverage.
tests_documented_added_justification: The test-and-coverage policy is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.
warnings_justification: TypeScript strict type-checking (`tsc --noEmit`) and a custom import-boundary linter run in CI.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any type error or boundary-rule violation, so warnings cannot merge to main.
warnings_strict_justification: Type and boundary checks are treated as errors (CI-blocking); the build is rejected on any finding.
know_secure_design_justification: The design applies secure-design principles: read-only by construction (Withe never runs Renovate, writes config, or merges), least privilege, loopback-by-default binding with an exposure warning when bound elsewhere without a password, optional TLS 1.2+ termination, constant-time HTTP Basic Auth, and log redaction of the admin token. These are documented in SECURITY.md.
know_common_errors_justification: Written in TypeScript (memory-safe); known-risk areas are guarded - input validation on CE identifiers, path-traversal defense (encodeURIComponent plus a boundary check), a redaction filter installed over console, and constant-time credential comparison. CodeQL and Trivy enforce this in CI.
crypto_published_justification: Withe uses only standard, published cryptography: optional TLS 1.2+ termination via Node.js/OpenSSL (WITHE_TLS_CERT/WITHE_TLS_KEY), and SHA-256 with timingSafeEqual (node:crypto) for constant-time credential comparison. No bespoke cryptography.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptographic functionality is delegated to the Node.js standard library - node:https/tls for TLS and node:crypto for hashing and constant-time comparison; nothing is reimplemented.
crypto_floss_justification: The Node.js crypto module (OpenSSL) is FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: When TLS termination is enabled, Withe sets a minimum of TLS 1.2 (src/tls-proxy/proxy.ts) and uses Node.js's default cipher configuration, whose key lengths meet or exceed the required minimums; the certificate and key are operator-supplied. Withe generates no keys of its own.
crypto_working_justification: No broken cryptographic algorithm is used for security. TLS is pinned to a 1.2 minimum with Node.js's secure default ciphers; SHA-256 is used only to equalize length for a constant-time compare, not to store passwords; no MD5, SHA-1, RC4, or single-DES is used for security.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptographic algorithm with known serious weaknesses is used for security purposes.
crypto_pfs_justification: When TLS termination is enabled (WITHE_TLS_CERT/WITHE_TLS_KEY), Withe uses Node.js's default TLS configuration with a TLS 1.2 minimum, whose ECDHE cipher suites provide perfect forward secrecy. When Withe runs behind a reverse proxy instead, the proxy provides transport security.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Withe stores no user-account passwords and has no user database. Access uses a single operator-supplied HTTP Basic Auth secret read from the environment or a mounted file, never stored by Withe, and compared in constant time.
crypto_random_justification: Withe's own code generates no security-sensitive random values (HTTP Basic Auth is stateless per request, with no sessions or tokens to mint); TLS handshake randomness is handled by Node.js/OpenSSL's CSPRNG.
delivery_mitm_justification: The container image is delivered over HTTPS (GHCR) and is cosign-signed (keyless Sigstore) with SLSA build provenance and a CycloneDX SBOM; release checksums are signed and the base image is pinned by digest - preventing MITM during retrieval.
delivery_unsigned_justification: The documented install path is `docker pull ghcr.io/schubydoo/withe` over HTTPS against a cosign-signed image; users are never directed to fetch unsigned code over HTTP.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities; dependencies are monitored with Renovate, GitHub security alerts, OSV-Scanner, and Trivy, and updated promptly (well within 60 days).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No unpatched critical vulnerabilities exist; the OpenSSF Scorecard Vulnerabilities check and code/dependency scanning run on pushes to main and on a schedule.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed; gitleaks and GitHub secret scanning run in CI, sensitive config is gitignored, CE fixtures are scrubbed against a denylist, and the redaction filter keeps the admin token out of logs and responses.
static_analysis_justification: Static analysis runs in CI: CodeQL (JavaScript/TypeScript), Trivy, zizmor (GitHub Actions auditing), gitleaks, OSV-Scanner, dependency-review, and OpenSSF Scorecard.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL targets common vulnerability classes for JavaScript/TypeScript.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Static-analysis findings are triaged and fixed before merge; the code-scanning alerts open before v1.0.0 were resolved prior to release.
static_analysis_often_justification: Static analysis runs on every pull request and push, with CodeQL and Scorecard also on a weekly schedule.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Property-based tests (fast-check) generate hundreds of inputs against the log-redaction filter's no-leak invariant on every CI run, and the full node --test suite exercises the running code offline.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Withe is written in TypeScript on Node.js, a memory-safe runtime; memory and behavior sanitizers for memory-unsafe languages do not apply.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The test suite exercises the code with assertions enabled throughout (node:assert).
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: There are no outstanding dynamic-analysis findings; the property and unit tests pass on main.
